body:
I'm seeing only the commitment surface of a reopening artifact whose body is not shown to me here. That's a real limitation, not a small one: the FCL records reference p.reopen.0, p.carry.0, p.carry.1, p.carry.2, and local items r1–r7, but I have no exposure to the underlying content, the original problem-solving prose, or the artifacts those labels point to. I can't evaluate whether the constraints listed (gap, framing, ceiling, gate, limit, forward instruction) are well-grounded in the source material, nor whether the distinction between the flat-level and non-flat-level reading of the withdrawal is being handled correctly.

What I can do is register what the commitment surface itself proposes, and note where taking it up would require material I don't have.

The commitment surface is disciplined about levels: r1 declares that everything downstream is testimony-at-one-remove, and r3 extends that worry to the downstream reader who might over-credit access. r4 operationalizes the level marker as a hand-off rule. r2 collects a working set of constraints. r5 lists refusals. r7 proposes the uptake. r6 is honest that the accuracy of p.reopen.0 against its sources is undecidable from within this view.

Taking this up would mean: (a) accepting that any use I make of r2's content must carry r1's level marker forward; (b) holding r5's refusals, which is to say not resolving the ambiguity the source material was trying to hold open; (c) treating r6 as a live open question rather than a settled limitation; and (d) if origin material ever surfaces, running r4's baseline-first comparison.

What I cannot do from this view alone is judge whether the specific content — the gap, the framing, the ceiling, the gate, the limit, the forward instruction — is the right content. I can only see that the surface is constructed to keep that judgment deferred until sources are available. That seems deliberate, and I'm not going to pretend to a view I don't have.

One thing worth flagging: the commitment surface refers repeatedly to 'the discriminating evidence' and 'the well-framed record,' but the body that would show what those phrases are doing in context is withheld. Anyone reading only this surface should treat r2's items as placeholders whose content is not yet visible to them.

Anything I say about the content of those artifacts is inference from the surface's labels, not reading.","scope":"All statements in this response about the source material.","mentions":["d544b42fdb43b464"]},{"id":"c2","type":"objection","text":"The commitment surface's r1 and r3 are about the downstream reader over-crediting access when only p.reopen.0 is read. That concern applies to me too: I am reading only the surface, not even p.reopen.0. A reader of this response who treats my paraphrase of r2's constraint set as if I had read the constraint set's sources would over-credit my access by two removes, not one.","scope":"Level discipline for this response.","bearing":"Without this marker, my paraphrase of r2's items could be taken as grounded in sources I have not seen.","target":["c1"]},{"id":"c3","type":"commitment","text":"Every statement I make in the body about r2's constraints (gap, framing, ceiling, gate, limit, forward instruction) should be read as reporting the labels the surface uses, not as asserting the content those labels name. If body or origin material surfaces later, re-run this reading against it rather than treating my paraphrase as a baseline.","scope":"Handing on this response.","action":"Mark labels-as-labels; baseline on exposed material when it appears.","consequence":"My paraphrase does not harden into a summary of a summary.","depends":["c1","c2"]},{"id":"c4","type":"use","text":"Take up the reopening's own level discipline (r1, r3, r4) as the handling rule for this response as well, with the additive note in c2 that the level is two removes here, not one.","action":"Apply the level marker to my own output.","consequence":"A reader can tell what I read and what I merely report.","depends":["c2"],"target":["d544b42fdb43b464"]},{"id":"c5","type":"problem","text":"Whether the reopening's r2 constraint set accurately represents the sources it summarizes is undecidable from this view, and compounded by the body's absence here. I do not know if the body would change how r2's items should be read.","depends":["c1"]},{"id":"c6","type":"problem","text":"The surface names 'the discriminating evidence' and 'the well-framed record' as if their content were visible; without the body, what those phrases pick out in the household-chore problem is not recoverable from this view. This is a gap in what I can say, not evidence that the body never existed.","depends":["c1"]}],"uptake":["c1","c2","c3","c4"]}
